That is a myth, and research shows that about 99% of the so-called colorblind people can see different colors. Because of this statistics, color blindness is not used to refer to those individuals on professional grounds. âColor Vision Deficiencyâ (CVD) has often been used as it is more accurate than the general âcolorblindness.â The statistics given by the color-blindness.com show that about 0.5% of women population (1 in 20) and 8% of men (1 in 12) are victims of color vision deficiency. CVD takes various forms which include Deuteranomalia (which makes the affected population to see things as a little bit fade), Protanopia (which makes things appear greenish), and Tritanopia (which is a greenish-pink vision).

pool.text: Color blindness is an inherited trait that can be passed on through reproduction but it has some peculiarities. It is recessive and not very prevalent in the gene pool. Because of this, color blindness does not appear very often in the population.
